comments.body:
**Resolution: complete matrix-theoretic proof written to `solution.tex`.**

There was no prior solution file; I wrote a full, self-contained proof of the Kharitonov vertex criterion using only matrix-theoretic tools (no appeal to Kharitonov's polynomial-coefficient theorem, no reduction to coefficient interlacing).

**Architecture (all steps carried out in full):**

1. **Lemma 1 (determinant).** `\chi_p(s)=det(sI-A(p))=p(s)` by cofactor expansion/induction; eigenvalues on `jR` iff `\chi_p(j\omega)=0`. This keeps everything inside the matrix family `\mathcal A`.

2. **Real/imag split.** `\chi_p(j\omega)=E_p(\omega)+jO_p(\omega)`, where `E_p` depends only on even-indexed coefficients and `O_p` only on odd-indexed ones, and (for `\omega>=0`) each coefficient's contribution has a sign fixed by `i mod 4`.

3. **Lemma 2 (value-set rectangle).** For each `\omega>=0`, `{\chi_p(j\omega):p in P}` is an axis-parallel rectangle whose four corners are exactly `\chi_{A_1},...,\chi_{A_4}` (verified: the four problem patterns are precisely the four corner sign-choices; same matrices for all `\omega`).

4. **Lemma 3 (Mikhailov / monotone phase).** `A(p)` Hurwitz iff `\chi_p(j\omega)\ne0` and `arg \chi_p(j\omega)` is strictly increasing with total `n\pi`. Proved directly from eigenvalue factorisation `prod(j\omega-\lambda_k)` and `\theta_k'(\omega)=\alpha_k/(\alpha_k^2+(\omega-\beta_k)^2)>0`. Converse via phase-change count `(n_- - n_+)\pi`.

5. **Lemma 4 (segment/edge lemma).** If two Hurwitz members differ only in even (resp. odd) coefficients, the whole segment is Hurwitz. Key step: at any common zero `\omega_j` of the shared odd part, both endpoints' real parts have sign `(-1)^j` (forced by phase monotonicity + `\phi(\omega_j)=j\pi`), so the connecting horizontal/vertical value segment misses 0; then a first-crossing/continuity argument propagates stability. This is the matrix Edge Theorem in dimension 1.

6. **Lemma 5 (zero exclusion).** If all four corners are Hurwitz, the four rectangle edges (each an even/odd segment between two Kharitonov vertices) are origin-free by Lemma 4; at `\omega=0` the rectangle sits in `Re>0` and for large `\omega` it escapes to infinity; a first-entry argument shows the origin can enter the rectangle only through its boundary — contradiction. Hence `0 \notin R(\omega)` for all `\omega`.

7. **Theorem.** Necessity is trivial. Sufficiency: zero-exclusion gives no member with imaginary eigenvalue; convexity of the coefficient box gives path-connectedness; a supremum/continuity argument from the Hurwitz vertex `A_1` propagates stability to every member.

**Verification performed (Python):** value set is the claimed rectangle with the four given patterns as corners; the segment lemma (even and odd versions) over thousands of random Hurwitz endpoint pairs (0 violations); the "same sign at common odd-part zeros" fact (0 violations); rectangle origin-exclusion under Hurwitz corners (0 violations); and full theorem end-to-end over thousands of random boxes, n=2..6 (0 mismatches). Degenerate intervals (`a_i^-=a_i^+`) and `n=1` are handled — no step divides by interval width.

LaTeX environment/reference/`$` balance checked programmatically (no toolchain available here to compile). A Remark documents how the same three ingredients (boundary-crossing, Mikhailov phase, segment lemma) extend to general convex matrix polytopes (Edge Theorem), as the problem requests.

Marking resolved.
